newsitem.title: UK: Barclays raises profit, to return capital.
newsitem.headline: Barclays raises profit, to return capital.

text.p: Barclays Plc, parent of Barclays Bank and investment bank BZW, on Tuesday said its 1996 pretax profits rose by 13 percent to 2.356 billion pounds ($3.8 billion).

Barclays said it would return 500 million pounds of excess capital to shareholders. It has already performed over one billion pounds of share repurchases in the last 18 months. ($ = 0.619 British Pounds)
Barclays said BZW saw a 29 percent fall in profits in 1996 -- to 204 million pounds from 289 million in 1995 -- affected by underperformance in both fixed income and foreign exchange trading.
In 1995, Barclays made a profit of 2.083 billion pounds. the 1996 figure includes a 70 million pound exceptional gain from business disposals.
The bank said it would a pay total dividend of 31.5p per share compared to 26p in 1995 and raised its earnings per share to 104.2p from 83.6.

"We have made significant progress throughout the group over the last few years in improving the nature and mix of our business," said Barclays chief executive Martin Taylor in a statement. "The continued high level and quality of our earnings are testimony to this progress."
